# 

Extremal number of 2-connected graphs avoiding cycles of length 2 modulo 2k

For integers $k\geq 3$k≥3 and sufficiently large $n$n, let $ex_2(n,\mathcal{C}_{2\bmod 2k})$e x 2​(n,C 2 mod 2 k​) denote the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected $n$n-vertex graph containing no cycle whose length is congruent to $2$2 modulo $2k$2 k.

Conjecture on the 2-connected extremal number.

$$ex_2(n,\mathcal{C}_{2\bmod 2k})=\binom{k}{2}+k(n-k)+1.$$e x 2​(n,C 2 mod 2 k​)=(2 k​)+k(n−k)+1.

Moreover, the extremal graph is

$$K_k\vee\bigl(K_2\cup (n-k-2)K_1\bigr).$$K k​∨(K 2​∪(n−k−2)K 1​).

This conjecture proposes the sharp edge count and a complete description of the extremal graph for the 2-connected setting. The source presents it as a conjecture for the general cases; no resolution is given there.

REMARKS.

(1) This is Problem 1.34 from [Kir97], posed by A. Casson.

(2) There is still no algorithm, but there have been some interesting computer-aided searches: Owens and Swenton search for ribbon bands for alternating knots [OS23] and Gukov, Halverson, Manolescu, and Ruehle apply machine learning algorithms to the problem [GHMR23]. Dunfield and Gong [DG25] have announced the results of a search for ribbon knots, slice knots, and concordances among the knots with at most 19 crossings.

(3) Casson and Long gave an algorithm to determine if a surface automorphism compresses [CL85]. In conjunction with the main results of [CG83a], this algorithm can be used to determine whether a given fibered knot bounds a fibered, homotopy-ribbon disk in a homotopy four-ball; see also [Lon86].
